name: Jadoh
ingredients: Red hill rice (Joha or local rice)
instructions: 1. Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pot and sauté sliced onions, bay leaves, ginger, and garlic paste until fragrant.
2. Add the pork pieces and cook until they are browned and tender.
3. Stir in the red rice and mix well to coat the grains with the pork fat and spices.
4. Pour in water (or stock) in a ratio appropriate for the rice and bring to a boil.
5. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer until the rice is fluffy and cooked through.
6. If using, fold in the pork blood towards the end to darken the rice and intensify the flavor, then steam until fully incorporated.
description: Jadoh is the quintessential comfort food of the Khasi community in Meghalaya. Historically prepared during celebrations and community gatherings, its name translates from 'Ja' (rice) and 'Doh' (meat). It is a beloved staple that reflects the rich, meat-centric culinary traditions of the Northeast hills.
